audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer treats Searing Charge's knockup as automatic: 'his Searing Charge knockup threatens any aggressive position' (mid), 'Use Brittle (passive) into Searing Charge knockup' (wants.foe[0]), 'he will knockup-interrupt the Devour' (late), 'his Searing Charge knockup punishes any greedy positioning' (whys[3]).
audit.why: Searing Charge only knocks up if Ornn COLLIDES WITH TERRAIN while charging. In open ground it is a dash that deals damage and nothing else. This is the single most actionable fact in the matchup and the content layer omits it entirely — the player is told to fear an ability he can disarm by choosing where to stand. Note the full layer already knows this ('Wall-knockup setup', 'Stand near walls for his Q' under Common Mistakes); the two layers contradict each other.
audit.corrected: No terrain, no knockup. Fight in open lane with walls off your back and Searing Charge is just a dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing explains where Ornn gets terrain in the middle of an open lane.
audit.why: Volcanic Rupture leaves a magma pillar at the end of its fissure, and that pillar is terrain. So Ornn manufactures his own wall: Q to plant the pillar, then E into it for the knockup. Telling the player to avoid walls is only half the rule — he also has to avoid the pillar Ornn just created, which is why 'dodge his Q' matters even after the initial damage is gone.
audit.corrected: Volcanic Rupture's pillar is terrain he can charge into. Dodging the Q is not just about the damage — it denies him the wall.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ornn.json Q Volcanic Rupture, E Searing Charge

audit.whatIsWrong: Ornn's passive is called 'Forgemaster' in five places (spikes[2], wants.foe[1], mid, whys[3], whys[5]) and Brittle is attributed to his passive in three (wants.foe[0] 'Use Brittle (passive)', early 'Ornn's passive Brittle', whys[0] 'his Brittle passive').
audit.why: His passive is Living Forge. Brittle comes from Bellows Breath (W) and from Call of the Forge God (R) — it is not passive and it is not always on, which means it is baitable. Neither wrong name was caught by the packet's detector.
audit.corrected: The passive is Living Forge. Brittle is applied by Bellows Breath and by the ultimate.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ornn.json P Living Forge, W Bellows Breath, R Call of the Forge God

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] and whys[5] explain Ornn's item lead as 'he finishes his first component faster than you' and 'his mythic arrives earlier via Forgemaster'.
audit.why: Living Forge does not make items cheaper or faster. It lets him buy anywhere, so he never surrenders lane tempo to a recall — that is where the timing edge actually comes from, and it is a different thing to play around. It also grants him additional bonus armour and magic resist from all sources, which is the real reason the tankiness gap widens as both of you buy resistances.
audit.corrected: He shops without walking home, so he never pays the recall tax; and every point of armour or MR he buys is worth more on him than on you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Call of the Forge God is described as a 'double knockup' that lands on cast (spikes[1], wants.foe[2], whys[4]).
audit.why: The elemental's first pass damages, slows and applies Brittle. The knockup only happens when Ornn recasts to charge into the elemental and redirect it back through you. There is a window between the two, and knowing the first pass is survivable is the difference between repositioning and giving up.
audit.corrected: First pass: damage, slow, Brittle. The knockup is the recast. Watch for Ornn charging the elemental, not just the elemental.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ornn.json R Call of the Forge God

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid, wants.you[2], wants.foe[2] and whys[4] all route level 6 through 'Abyssal Voyage' and its 'pool'.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-rework ultimate and is not in the current kit. Level 6 gives Devour. The reposition is Abyssal Dive (W) from level 2, 21s at rank 1. wants.foe[2] in particular tells the player his escape is on a cooldown he does not have.
audit.corrected: Level 6 gives Devour; Abyssal Dive is the reposition and is 21s.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] and content.late teach 'your 3-stack stun into Devour combo' as one action, and content.late says to save it 'for when his E pillar is on cooldown' — the pillar is Q, the charge is E.
audit.why: Tongue Lash on a three-stack target stuns and consumes the stacks; devouring an enemy champion requires three stacks. Against two full tanks where stacks are scarce, spending them twice is not available. The pillar/charge slot mix-up also sends the player watching the wrong cooldown.
audit.corrected: Three stacks buys the stun or the Devour. Volcanic Rupture (Q) makes the pillar; Searing Charge (E) is the dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers repeat 'trade around Volcanic Rupture's cooldown' without ever giving a number.
audit.why: This is the losing matchup in the slice at 48.80%, and the entire plan is stated as waiting for cooldowns whose lengths are never supplied.
audit.corrected: Volcanic Rupture 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s at 800. Bellows Breath 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s. Searing Charge 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s at 450. Call of the Forge God 140/120/100s. Your Tongue Lash is 900, longer than any of his non-ultimate ranges.

audit.why: 48.80% over 957 games with a chart of Ornn 4 / Skill 3 / Tahm Kench 0. A losing matchup with no Tahm Kench stage is internally consistent, and the packet flagged no contradiction. Left alone.

edits.before: At levels 1 through 3 this is a slow, attritional poke lane — Tongue Lash's range is your best tool, but Ornn's passive Brittle makes every trade dangerous if you let him proc it with Bellows Breath before you land your stun. Fish for An Acquired Taste stacks with Q from distance, and only commit to the stun-into-Devour window if he wastes Searing Charge or misses his E pillar entirely. Thick Skin is converting poke passively from the first auto, so don't panic if he procs Brittle once — idle outside his E range and let the grey health heal back before you re-engage.
edits.after: At levels 1 through 3 this is a slow, attritional poke lane — Tongue Lash's 900 is your best tool, and Brittle comes from Bellows Breath rather than any passive, which means it is baitable rather than always on. Fish for An Acquired Taste stacks with Q from distance, and only spend three of them if he has wasted Searing Charge or missed the Volcanic Rupture pillar that gives it terrain. Thick Skin converts poke from the first auto, so don't panic at one Brittle — idle outside his 450 and let the grey health come back.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 belong to Ornn. He is farming efficiently with Forgemaster components ticking ahead of your build, his Searing Charge knockup threatens any aggressive position, and without Abyssal Voyage you have no escape if he hits a Call of the Forge God. Play for the wave and save Tongue Lash as a reactive slow rather than a stack-fishing tool — if you burn Q and miss, his entire knockup combo window opens. At 6 you gain global threat with R, so start rotating bot rather than forcing a lane kill you are unlikely to convert.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 belong to Ornn. Living Forge keeps him shopping without ever leaving lane, and Searing Charge threatens any position with terrain behind it — but only positions with terrain behind them, which is the one lever you actually hold in this lane. Play for the wave and save Tongue Lash as a reactive slow rather than a stack-fishing tool; if you burn Q and miss, his whole combo window opens. At 6 you gain Devour, not a map tool, so look for the three-stack window rather than a rotation you cannot convert.

edits.before: Late game both of you are near-unkillable frontliners and the matchup becomes pure teamfight positioning. Your 3-stack stun into Devour is the only reliable way to remove Ornn from a fight — but only use it when his Searing Charge is on cooldown, or he will knockup-interrupt the Devour and put you on both CD timers simultaneously. Peel your carries from his R double knockup with Devour on your own backline; your job is not to kill Ornn, it is to make sure his engage never reaches your damage dealers.
edits.after: Late game both of you are near-unkillable frontliners and the matchup becomes pure teamfight positioning. Three stacks spent on Devour is the only reliable way to remove Ornn from a fight — spend them where Searing Charge has no wall and no pillar to reach, because a knockup off terrain interrupts you. Peel your carries with Devour on your own backline; on an ally it costs no stacks at all. Your job is not to kill Ornn, it is to keep his engage off your damage dealers.

notes: This is the one losing matchup in the slice (48.80%) and its most valuable fact was missing from the layer players read. Searing Charge only knocks up on terrain collision, and Volcanic Rupture's pillar is the terrain Ornn manufactures for it — the content layer presented the knockup as unconditional in four places while the full layer already had it right ('Wall-knockup setup', 'Stand near walls for his Q'). The two layers were teaching opposite things about the same ability; worth checking whether that split runs across other Ornn entries in the file. Second champion-wide item: Ornn's passive is Living Forge, called 'Forgemaster' five times here and never flagged by the packet's name detector, and Brittle is attributed to his passive three times when it comes from Bellows Breath and the ultimate. Also note spikes[2] and whys[5] referred to Ornn's 'mythic' item — mythic items are legacy terminology and I removed it from both strings rather than reasoning about the current item system, which I cannot verify from the kit files. The 'Abyssal Voyage' problem reported in tahmkench__mel.json affects four strings here, including wants.foe[2], which told the player his escape was on a cooldown for an ability he does not have. No WKM_LINES errors observed for this matchup.
